prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, using bifunctional PROTAC molecules to direct the ubiquitin-proteasome system to chosen proteins

statement.case_for: I have moved my preferred configuration from B069 plus B052 to B067 alone, with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. The scientific reason is that PROTACs are a physical mechanism that was designed and then measured: a bifunctional molecule forms a ternary complex, the cooperativity and linker dependence of that complex can be quantified, and Ciulli's crystal structures of VHL-ligand and ternary complexes explain why some degraders work and others do not. That is mechanism made visible, which is what I value. The principle has been reproduced in many laboratories and now gives researchers something they could not do before, namely acute and selective removal of a protein. Crews and Deshaies hold the priority for the concept, and Ciulli holds the structure-guided step that turned it into drug-like chemistry. A citation limited to bifunctional PROTACs and the ubiquitin-proteasome system can be defended with three names without claiming more than they support.
statement.case_against: Two problems remain. First, the molecular-glue strand (Handa and Ito on cereblon, with Sakamoto, Kim, Gray and others) is a different origin and is not covered by this trio. I would keep the citation strictly to heterobifunctional molecules and say nothing that implies glues, so the committee does not appear to merge two discoveries. Second, no degrader is yet approved, so the clinical consequence is prospective. I do not think that alone should decide the matter, because the chemistry and the mechanism are already established and widely used as a tool, but I accept that it could look early. I also drop the B069 plus B052 pairing. The two parts were unrelated, base editing sits near the 2020 CRISPR prize, and a single coherent prize is the better public statement.

responses.point: Chabes keeps Crews and Deshaies but names Handa as third, arguing that cereblon links the PROTAC and glue branches into one achievement. He also asked me what experimental result would settle the nitrogenase mechanism.
responses.response: On nitrogenase, I cannot name a single result that would settle the catalytic mechanism today. Trapping and structurally defining the intermediates of the E4 state would be the minimum, and until that exists you and Zou are right that it is not ready. That is why it is only my second alternative now. On the third B067 name, I do not think cereblon makes the branches one achievement. Cereblon explains thalidomide-type glues and was later used as a PROTAC ligase, but the PROTAC concept and the structure-guided design rules came from a different line. If the committee prefers Handa, then the citation has to be rewritten around the glue mechanism and the prize becomes a different one. I prefer to cite the PROTAC achievement cleanly and accept that Handa and Ito are left out, which I regret.

responses.point: Aqvist supports Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli with a quantitative argument: ternary-complex cooperativity, linker design and structure-guided VHL ligands. He also questions whether Gray and Winkler (B069) are a separate achievement from Marcus theory (1992).
responses.response: I agree with the quantitative argument and it is the main reason I now support this configuration. His point on B069 is fair. The Marcus prize covers the theoretical frame, and what Gray and Winkler added is the experimental distance and driving-force dependence in proteins and the pathway picture, which is a biological extension. The expert report might judge that as a deepening, not a new principle, and I cannot argue that it is a game-changer by the standard he and Zou apply. Since my own research is adjacent to that field, I am also content not to carry it as my preferred part. He also notes that if glues and PROTACs are one achievement then his trio weakens. I think they are two achievements, so the trio stays valid with a PROTAC-only citation.

responses.point: Aili wrote that the concept is original, that Crews and Deshaies lead, and that the drug-like realisation through Ciulli's design work is a molecular design story. Elsewhere he raises how much of degrader chemistry is new beyond linker and ligand optimization.
responses.response: In round 1 I asked the expert report to say whether PROTACs and glues are one achievement or two. Having read the group's statements, I think the evidence points to two, and I find his design-story framing for the PROTAC side adequate. On his own doubt about novelty beyond optimization, I would answer that the new element is the ternary complex as the central object. Its cooperativity is a measurable property that can be designed, and that goes beyond tuning a linker. I withdraw my earlier statement that clinical validation incomplete was a reason to keep B067 as an alternative only.

responses.point: Somfai prefers Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B013) for its maturity and clean two-person credit, and acknowledges that the 2010 prize may make it look like an extension.
responses.response: I understand the appeal of a mature method with a clean credit, and I would not call B013 weak. My difficulty is the same one he states: it must show a distinct achievement from 2010, and I see ligand design and mechanism here as an extension in a field already recognised. B067 has the greater change of capability, and its maturity is sufficient in my view, since the concept dates from 2001 and has two decades of independent confirmation. It is a close call on attribution, not on science.

responses.point: Linke ranked phase separation first in the opening round and now supports B067, and in the chair's questions asks what specifically keeps B067 from being the first choice for Brzezinski, Somfai and Sparr.
responses.response: To answer the chair's question directly, what kept B067 from first place for me was the attribution of the third name and the glue question, not the science. I think both are resolved by a PROTAC-only citation with Ciulli, and the absence of an approved drug should not decide it. On B049, my view is unchanged. I would want in vivo evidence that the liquid-like state is functionally essential, and the citation would have to be written very narrowly. I do not think it is ready this year.

uncertainties: Whether the expert report treats PROTACs and thalidomide-type glues as two achievements, as I now assume, and whether leaving out Handa, Ito, Gray, Sakamoto and Kim would be accepted.
Whether Ciulli or Handa should be the third name. I judge Ciulli by the structural and design evidence, but I hold this less firmly than the rest of the configuration.
How the absence of an approved degrader will be read in 2026, since I am not certain of the current clinical status.
Whether Gray and Winkler (B069) are a separable achievement from Marcus theory. I set this aside, but it could return if B067 fails to carry a majority.
statement.conflict_note: My research on respiratory proton and electron transfer is adjacent to Gray and Winkler (B069) and to nitrogenase (B036), so I have no objection to the committee judging whether I should recuse on those parts. Because my preferred configuration is now B067, that proximity no longer affects my preferred position. I have no specific conflict with Crews, Deshaies or Ciulli. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, which has no bearing on any shortlisted candidate.
